corpus.tags: common thesis physical systems observation sensing data intelligence hardware
corpus.text: The common thesis is not robotics plus space for their own sake. Both companies use difficult physical systems to capture information that is expensive or unreliable to obtain today. The venture outcome appears only if that information compounds into a recurring decision layer.

corpus.tags: robotic NDT UT PAUT TOFD tanks pipelines weld inspection
corpus.text: Octobotics publicly offers robotic inspection workflows for industrial assets and describes ultrasonic NDT capabilities including UT, PAUT and TOFD.

corpus.tags: petrobot competition certification ATEX PESO ONGC HPCL
corpus.text: PetroBot is a serious Indian competitor. It publicly states hazardous-area certifications and strategic backing from oil and gas companies.

corpus.tags: petrobot better investment competitor why invest octobotics
corpus.text: PetroBot's progress is category validation, not a reason to pretend competition is absent. Octobotics is investable only if the earlier entry point plus future certification, platform reuse, customer expansion or geography creates enough upside. If post-certification differentiation is weak, the thesis becomes an execution-and-price bet.

corpus.tags: walk away linear headcount services margin
corpus.text: The master kill criterion is linearity: if inspection capacity and revenue can only grow by adding field engineers and robots in roughly the same proportion, Octobotics remains an industrial services business rather than a venture-scale technology platform.

corpus.tags: data moat analytics asset health predictive maintenance
corpus.text: A data / asset-health layer is upside, not base-case underwriting. Repeated digital inspections could eventually support condition trends and predictive maintenance, but this only matters if Octobotics has sufficient reuse rights and customers actually pay for the intelligence layer.

corpus.tags: founder questions diligence certification platform reuse field engineer
corpus.text: The highest-information diligence questions are job-level contribution margin, percentage of platform reuse when entering a new vertical, dated certification milestones and whether inspection output can grow faster than field headcount.

corpus.tags: Varuna orbit demonstrator SAR AIS constellation 30 minute revisit
corpus.text: PierSight says its Varuna demonstrator completed primary mission objectives in orbit. Its public target state is a maritime SAR+AIS constellation; the full network is not yet deployed.

corpus.tags: MATSYA analytics dashboard SAR AIS optical terrestrial
corpus.text: PierSight describes MATSYA as a maritime intelligence layer that combines SAR, AIS and other data sources into monitoring, alerts and query workflows.

corpus.tags: non linear recurring analytics revenue per satellite scaling
corpus.text: PierSight becomes non-linear when recurring intelligence revenue grows faster than satellite count. That requires overlapping observations to support multiple paid workflows—security, insurance, compliance and trading—instead of every incremental dollar consuming equivalent new tasking capacity.

corpus.tags: Bloomberg ocean end state customers coast guard insurer bank trader
corpus.text: The end-state is ‘Bloomberg for the ocean’: a common maritime intelligence layer where a Coast Guard buys threat intelligence, an insurer buys behavioural risk, a bank buys sanctions intelligence, and a trader buys physical-flow signals from overlapping observation infrastructure.

corpus.tags: walk away imagery utility capital intensity satellite count
corpus.text: The thesis weakens sharply if MATSYA remains a dashboard and revenue stays priced per image, per tasking or per kilometre of coverage. In that case growth remains tied to capital expenditure and PierSight behaves like an imagery utility.

corpus.tags: third party imagery MATSYA analytics own satellites
corpus.text: MATSYA being able to ingest third-party data is not a problem by itself. The key test is whether PierSight's own observations and historical data measurably improve latency, accuracy, prediction or unit economics. Owning satellites must create an advantage, not an artificial technical dependency.

corpus.tags: competition ICEYE incumbent maritime SAR dark vessels
corpus.text: Global SAR incumbents already validate maritime surveillance, so PierSight should not be underwritten on novelty of SAR or dark-vessel detection. Its case rests on maritime-specific economics and turning observation into recurring intelligence.

corpus.tags: founder questions diligence satellite 5 15 32 economics third party data
corpus.text: The highest-information diligence questions are when recurring revenue switches on as the constellation scales, the measurable advantage of the maritime architecture, how many paid workflows can reuse an observation, and what MATSYA gains from PierSight's own data versus third-party feeds.
